entries.title: Siren

emulation.emulator: Sony Classics emulator; PCSX2 for owned-disc preservation
emulation.notes: Prefer the official PS5/PS4 Classics release for a current official route. PCSX2 remains useful for owned-disc preservation testing.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official up-rendered PS2 presentation with rewind, quick save, and video-filter features.

primary.why: The current PlayStation Store release is the best official route because it preserves the PS2 original while adding up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and custom video filters.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Siren from the PlayStation Store or access it through PlayStation Plus Premium where available, then play on PS5 or PS4. Use PCSX2 with an owned PS2 copy only for preservation comparison.

all_releases.reason: skip: complete original version, but the current PlayStation Store Classics release is the best official modern route.
skip: official older digital route, but superseded by the newer PlayStation Store Classics version with added convenience features.

all_releases.fidelity: Official Classics release with up-rendering, rewind, quick save, and custom video filters.
all_releases.reason: primary: best official modern route and no sourced content loss versus the PS2 original.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The current PlayStation Store Classics release is the original PS2 game with official emulator enhancements; no content loss was identified.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is an enhanced/emulated classic release, not a remake or asset-level remaster.

entries.title: Forbidden Siren 2

emulation.notes: PCSX2 is the practical high-resolution capture route for an owned PAL or Japanese PS2 copy.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS2 assets and presentation with emulator-side resolution and filtering improvements.

primary.why: Forbidden Siren 2 is a PlayStation 2-only sequel that was released in Japan, Europe, and Australia but not North America, with no sourced official remaster or modern rerelease.
primary.how_to_play: Play an owned PAL or Japanese PS2 copy on compatible PS2 hardware, or use PCSX2 with an owned copy for cleaner capture.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PS2 release; PCSX2 can improve capture resolution from an owned copy.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced commercial platform, preserving the complete original release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No alternate release with higher official fidelity or exclusive content was identified.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced official remaster, remake, PC port, North American release, or modern rerelease was identified.

entries.title: Siren: Blood Curse

emulation.notes: Original PS3 hardware is the straightforward official route. RPCS3 can be used only for owned-copy preservation testing if compatibility is acceptable.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original PS3 presentation, with possible emulator-side improvements if RPCS3 handles the owned copy well.

primary.why: Siren: Blood Curse is a PS3-only reimagining of the first Siren; the complete Blu-ray/episodes 1-12 route keeps the full game together, while the Blu-ray edition is documented as including extra behind-the-scenes material.
primary.how_to_play: Use the PS3 Blu-ray release where available, or buy/download Episodes 1-12 from the PlayStation Store on PS3 if still accessible for the account.

all_releases.fidelity: PSN episodic release sold as Episodes 1-12.
all_releases.reason: skip: complete digital game route, but the Blu-ray collection is cleaner for archival play and has sourced bonus video material.

all_releases.fidelity: Complete PS3 Blu-ray collection with all 12 episodes and documented bonus behind-the-scenes/interview material.
all_releases.reason: primary: complete disc route for the PS3-only game, with the most complete package of playable episodes plus bonus material.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Both PSN and Blu-ray routes contain the full playable game; the Blu-ray package is selected for cleaner archival completeness and bonus material.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a reimagining of Siren, not a straight remaster of the PS2 original, and should be treated as its own game.
